p:cNvPr.descr: Image of different types of cells, spanning from normal to cancerous, from ages 30-50, 40-60, and 50-70. Image of different types of cells, spanning from normal to cancerous, from ages 30-50, 40-60, and 50-70. At the top of the image, there is a series of light green and pink boxes, labeled "genes." The first green box reads, "MMR (DNA repair); the second pink box reads, "APC Beta-catenin." There's a space between the second and third box. The third box, which is also light green and slightly larger than the fourth box, is labeled, "CDC4 (ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis); the fourth box is labeled, "KRAS BRAF." There's another space between the fourth and fifth boxes. The fifth box, whixh is light green, reads, "PI3K." The sixth and seventh boxes, both light pink, reads, "TP53 (P53) and SMAD4 TGFBR2," respectively. Below the genes, theres a tannish layer of cells, separated by an orange layer in the middle and lined by a darker layer on top. The darker layer on top is labeled "Epitelium," the middle layer is labeled "smooth muscle," and the tannish layers are labeled "connective tissue." An arrow pointing upward to the next group of cells is labeled, "Age 30-50." The arrow points to a similar structure as previously described, but this time, the orange layer on top is pulled up, forming a little tree with a bulb at the top. This is labeled "Small adenoma." An arrow next to it is labeled "Age 40-60" and points upward to a similar structure with an even larger tree and bulb at the top. This is labeled "Large adenoma." An arrow pointing upward is labeled "Age 50-70" and poits up to an even larger strucutre with a tall tree and big bulb at the top. The right side of the bulb is shaded pink, and a white arrow is dram in this area. This last structure is labeled "Cancer." Next to this is an arrow pointing to a diagram of the human body with the heart, lungs, and digestive system show. Two red arrows start in the colon at a small red ball. One arrow points to the liver while the other points to the lungs. This diagram is labeled "Metastasis." Below this drawing is a series of green and red arrows. This schematic is labeled "Growth factor." Starting from left to right, there is a gree arrow labeled COX-2. In front of this is the back of a red arrow, labeled 15-PGDH. Below these two structures is a green arrow pointing to the right and labeled EGFR (epidermal growth factor receptor). Below this is the back of a red arrow, labeled TGF-beta (tumor growth factor). The back of the red arrows are labeled "Tumor suppressor factors turned off in colon cancer." The two gree arrows are labeled "Oncogenic mediators turned on in colon cancer."
